title: GO Command Center Deploy Readiness V1
description: A read-only answer to whether a deploy can proceed now, and if not why not. It combines the derived control state with an operator-supplied read-only bundle of live-host facts and the published verifier identities, re-derives the live Boss Request Bridge bundle acceptance rules, and returns DEPLOY_READY = YES / NO / UNKNOWN with the concrete blocking reasons. Every gate is mandatory: CANARY and RELEASE_GATES block because the live Bridge blocks on them, and BRIDGE_ACCEPTANCE exists so that YES can only be reported when the live gate would accept the same request. It never creates or publishes a DEPLOY Task, never opens the request switch, accepts no caller-controlled parameter, and does not touch Production. A readiness verdict is an observation about the current evidence, never an authorisation to deploy.

as_of.description: the instant the gates were evaluated at; supplied, never read from the clock implicitly

deploy_ready.description: YES only when every mandatory gate PASSes. NO when any mandatory gate FAILs. UNKNOWN otherwise, because an unprovable mandatory gate is never an inferred yes.

state.description: UNKNOWN is the only honest state for a mandatory live fact nobody could establish. It is never promoted to PASS.

blocking_reasons.description: One entry per mandatory gate that is not PASS, in gate order. Never empty when the verdict is not YES.

advisory_holds.description: Advisory gates that did not PASS. They never change the verdict and are never hidden, so an operator can see that a declared gate is still, for example, HOLD.

rollback_readiness.description: CC V1-09 / #104 owns rollback eligibility. This evaluator answers deploy readiness only and says so instead of guessing.

roles.description: One entry per published signing role the plan contract distinguishes. A role whose binding is not BOUND may not be used to claim anything.

approval_identities.description: The GitHub logins this project authorises as the V1 Human Approval authority. The authority is an authenticated identity rather than a published key, so it is carried as an allowlist and an approval is judged on the identity it names.

may_read_live_command_center_state.description: the only thing it may do with live facts: read the operator's read-only bundle, never contact the host itself

is_a_deploy_approval.description: YES is not an approval. Human Approval is a separate, named gate and the only thing that can carry one

x-go-gates.note: The closed gate set. Every gate is mandatory: a gate the live Bridge blocks on cannot be advisory here without letting this document disagree with the live gate. advisory_holds therefore exists as a stable field and is always empty.

APPROVED_CANDIDATE.meaning: an approved candidate exists and is a complete RELEASE_CANDIDATE_V1: the contract owned by the candidate admission component, whose block must carry every required identity. A pointer that only names a commit is not deployable.

SOURCE_BINDING.meaning: the candidate own source identity is complete, well-formed, and agrees with the RELEASE_CANDIDATE_V1 block it carries about the commit, application tree and fingerprint

PACKAGE_BINDING.meaning: the deployment plan candidate identity equals the candidate, the plan approves the artifact the RELEASE_CANDIDATE_V1 claims, and the image/repo-digest pairing is internally consistent

DEPLOYMENT_PLAN.meaning: an approved plan exists for the release and its own fields pass the live Bridge plan rules

HUMAN_APPROVAL.meaning: an unexpired approval binding the same plan digest, scope and environment, naming one of the GitHub identities this project authorises as the Human Approval authority

TEST_PR.meaning: the candidate source commit has a signed TEST_PR result on the control bus

VERIFY.meaning: the live runtime was verified by signed Evidence inside the freshness window, and the plan own preflight proof would be accepted by the live Bridge

CURRENT_RUNTIME.meaning: the verified live runtime matches the image the plan expects to be current, so there is no drift

LIVE_SWITCH.meaning: the live Command Center request switch state; a live-host fact

LIVE_SWITCH_PROVENANCE.meaning: the switch state is covered by a change record signed by the distinct Human Approval authority, whose declared value equals the observed channel value and whose window is still open

CANARY.meaning: the plan canary proof verifies under the published identities, binds to this candidate and completed inside the canary window

RELEASE_GATES.meaning: the plan carries PASS for every release gate the live contract requires

BRIDGE_ACCEPTANCE.meaning: the live Boss Request Bridge own bundle rules, re-derived offline from the same inputs, would accept this request

x-go-verdict-rules: A mandatory gate that FAILs makes the verdict NO, whatever else says otherwise.
A mandatory gate that cannot be established makes the verdict UNKNOWN. It is never rounded up to YES, and it never becomes an inferred approval.
YES requires every mandatory gate to PASS, and it still authorises nothing: it means the evidence currently supports deploying, not that anyone has agreed to.
YES may never be reported while the live Bridge would deterministically refuse the same request. BRIDGE_ACCEPTANCE is the gate that makes this impossible, not a convention.
A switch that is on without a change record attributed to the Human Approval authority keeps LIVE_SWITCH_PROVENANCE out of PASS, and therefore keeps the verdict out of YES.
advisory_holds exists for contract stability and is always empty: no gate is advisory.
x-go-forbidden: Creating, signing or publishing a DEPLOY Task.
Opening, arming or toggling the DEPLOY request switch or the channel configuration.
Any caller-supplied image, service, service list, path, compose file, environment file, shell command, executor path or signing parameter.
Contacting Command Center or Hong Kong directly: only the operator read-only bundle, the derived state and the published identities are read.
Reporting YES while a mandatory gate is UNKNOWN, or while a gate it could not read exists.
Reporting YES while the live Boss Request Bridge would refuse the same request.
Clamping CANARY or RELEASE_GATES to advisory, or otherwise letting this evaluator block less than the live gate does.
Treating a published signing key, or an approval that names an identity outside the authorised GitHub set, as a Human Approval authority.
